alerts.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued August 25 at 5:15PM MDT until August 25 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
continue to be possible over the Aspen Acres burn scar.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Colorado, including the following
areas, Pueblo Vicinity/Pueblo County Below 6300 Feet, Wet Mountains
Above 10000 Feet and Wet Mountains between 6300 and 10000 Feet.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Aspen Acres burn scar is expected
up to and during the period of the watch. Residents near the Aspen
Acres burn scar should prepare for potential debris flow. Be sure
to stay up to date with information from local authorities. Heavy
rainfall could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas, urbanized
street flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall over the burn scar, which may lead to flash flooding and
debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Pueblo, Pueblo Airport, Boone, Salt Creek, Blende, Pueblo
Reservoir, Pueblo West, Avondale, Pinon, Pueblo Depot, Greenhorn
Mountain, Silver Cliff, Rye, Colorado City, Beulah, San Isabel
and Rosita.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 25 at 5:07PM MDT until August 25 at 7:45PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
At 507 PM MDT, emergency management reported thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Between 0.7 and 1.5
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.1 to 0.5
inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is already
occurring. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in
debris flow moving through the North Saint Charles, South Creek,
Squirrel Creek, Middle Creek, and North Creek Drainages. The debris
flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Middle Aspen Acres Burn
Scar.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported 6-12 inches of water and
debris flowing down north creek and north creek cutoff at
501 pm.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Beulah.

This includes the following high risk locations...
Beulah Water Intake, Northcreek Road county line to Red Mountain Camp
and Northcreek Road from Red Mountain Camp to Beulah.

alerts.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 25 at 4:30PM MDT until August 25 at 7:30PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Northern Aspen Acres Burn Scar in...
Eastern Custer County in southeastern Colorado...
West Central Pueblo County in southeastern Colorado...

* Until 730 PM MDT.

* At 430 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Northern Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Between 0.2 and
0.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.2
to 0.5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the
burn scar will result in debris flow moving through the Red Creek,
Peck Creek and Rock Creek Drainages. The debris flow can consist of
rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Northern Aspen Acres Burn
Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Northern Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Eastern Custer and West Central Pueblo
Counties.
